conviction_note: A slight positive lean (p_up 54) on an abs move of 8.5 (implied 7.89 is indicative only because the ATM spread is 47% of mid; median own reaction 7.35; one-analyst coverage; a new Q3 guide is coming) gives +0.68. The findings sum to +0.6. The two numbers agree because the evidence is thin, mostly in the wire, and balanced: the company's own GE figures imply an H2 step-up that should support the Q3 guide, against freight and supply caveats and a summer slowdown at Airbus. This stock trades on the next-quarter range: +7.35 on an in-range Q1 with a higher Q2 range, -12.47 after a record Q4 with a lower Q1 range. So the sign is decided by a guide nobody outside the company has seen, and p_up stays near 50.
bar: Company Q2 FY27 range of $19.5-21.0m sales (midpoint $20.25m) and $4.3-5.1m adj. EBITDA, given on the 2026-07-20 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15261981797278720). Estimate sources disagree: Chartmill $19.54m / $0.13 EPS (https://www.chartmill.com/news/PKE/Chartmill-51213-Park-Aerospace-Corp-NYSEPKE-Surges-After-Strong-Earnings-Beat) and Benzinga $20.0m / $0.16 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PKE/earnings-forecasts). The company guide is the bar. Q1 landed at the top of its own range ($18.31m against $17.7-18.4m), and I expect Q2 to land inside its range, slightly above the midpoint.
positioning_check: Short interest is 1.1M shares and 4.34 days to cover at the 2026-07-15 FINRA settlement, up from 1.3M shares and 2.2 days at 06-30 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/pke/short-interest/). findings.finding: The company's own GE Aerospace figures imply a second-half step-up. GE engine program sales were $7.1m in Q1 and are estimated at $7.5-8.25m for Q2, with roughly $34-38m for FY27 (the transcript reads 34.38). That leaves about $19-23m for Q3+Q4, or roughly $9.5-11.5m a quarter against about $7.9m in Q2. This supports a Q3 sales range at or above the Q2 range, which is the line this stock trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The next-quarter range has decided the last two prints: Q1 FY27 (2026-07-20) came in at the top of its range with a higher Q2 range, and the stock rose 7.35%. Q4 FY26 (2026-05-28) printed a record $24.2m, but the Q1 range of $17.7-18.4m was a step down, and the stock fell 12.47% (baseline; Q4 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000076267/000143774926018758/ex_969292.htm).
findings.why_not_priced: The FY GE number was said on the call. Subtracting H1 to get the H2 run-rate is arithmetic, and the one-analyst coverage does not appear to have done it: consensus Q2 sales of $19.54-20.0m sit at or below the bottom half of the company range. If the step-up were priced, the stock would not sit 21% under its August high with a flat 20-day run-up. It stays small because the GE number comes from the customer, which the company says it 'haircut', and timing is the customer's ('Customers decide everything').
findings.independence: Safran, after Park spoke, said CFM delivered 1,030 LEAP engines in H1 2026 (+41%) and expects more than 2,000 for 2026 (https://centreforaviation.com/news/cfm-to-deliver-more-than-2000-leap-engines-in-2026-safran-ceo-1356585). This is an industry proxy and not Park's own number.

findings.finding: Hexcel's Q2 2026 results came out on 2026-07-29, after Park last spoke. Commercial aerospace sales rose 18.3%, narrowbody sales (A320neo, 737 MAX) grew, and full-year sales and EPS guidance were raised. Hexcel says it ships materials 4-6 months ahead of aircraft deliveries, so its order flow covers Park's June-August quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reported-quarter sales inside the company's own range have been bought when the next range rose (+7.35, 2026-07-20) and sold when it fell (-12.47, 2026-05-28). The quarter alone has not moved the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer print landing after Park's own guide is the kind of read-through that a one-analyst name does not reprice. If the market had priced it, Park would not have drifted from about $37 to $30 while a composite peer was raising guidance. It is a proxy, though: Park's quarter is set by its own customers' order timing, and the range already assumed growth.
findings.independence: Safran's LEAP statement points the same way (https://centreforaviation.com/news/cfm-to-deliver-more-than-2000-leap-engines-in-2026-safran-ceo-1356585). It is a different source and also a proxy.

findings.finding: On or about 2026-08-04, after Park's 2026-07-20 call, Lockheed received a seven-year PAC-3 MSE multiyear award of up to $53.86bn (total $58.62bn) to triple capacity by 2030. Park is the sole-source qualified supplier of ablative composite materials for the PAC-3 MSE solid rocket motor, so the award firms the missile leg of any forward commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Missile commentary alone has no isolated reaction in the baseline. The May 2026 call already quoted the customer's 'more than 2,000' PAC-3 rate, and the stock still fell 12.47% that day on the quarter range.
findings.source_date: 2026-08-04 (Joint Forces reprints the same release as 2026-07-29)
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the award is public and Park had already framed the PAC-3 ramp. What may be new is a firmer multi-year statement from Park on tonight's call. This is small because it lands beyond the window economically, and Q2 shipment timing is set by the motor maker.
findings.independence: The Army's own note on the accelerated production contract (https://www.army.mil/article/291670) is the same program and does not add independent evidence about Park.

findings.finding: Q2 risks: on the 2026-07-20 call management said it was 'a little concerned' that supply chain and international freight could hit Q2. Separately, Airbus delivered only 57 aircraft in August (67 in July, 89 in June) and is behind pace on its 870 target.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There has been no below-range quarter in the visible history. The -5.29 on 2025-10-09 (Q2 FY26) is the closest analogue of a soft Q2.
findings.why_not_priced: The freight caveat is in the transcript, and the range was set with it in mind, so this lands inside the guide and is sized near zero. The Airbus slowdown is a narrow delivery proxy. Hexcel's broader materials series says the 4-6-month-ahead supply chain was still building, so the slowdown is sized below that series.
findings.independence: Airbus August deliveries (https://rotatepilot.com/news/airbus-boosts-august-deliveries-9-but-remains-behind-pace-for-870-aircraft-2026--2026-09-07). This is a different source and a narrow proxy.

findings.finding: The finance and operations bench turned over around this quarter. On 2026-07-15 the company filed an NT 10-Q for the May quarter, citing time to finish closing procedures. The corporate controller died suddenly (announced 2026-07-21). A new CFO was elected on 2026-08-13, and the SVP/GM changed on 2026-07-10. This is the first close under the new finance team, which raises some risk of a messy release or another late filing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline. The July NT 10-Q was followed by an on-time release and a +7.35 reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The filings are public, but nothing in the price or coverage reflects any control-risk discount. It is small because the release date was confirmed in the normal way (2026-10-05), which suggests the close went to schedule.
findings.independence: EDGAR filing list showing the NT 10-Q (2026-07-15) and the 8-K Item 5.02 filings of 07-09 and 08-17 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000076267&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40). The underlying facts are the same.

findings.finding: Insiders sold into strength after the Q1 print. The COO exercised and sold 60,000 shares at $33.11 on 2026-07-29, keeping 15,000 directly. The CEO exercised and sold 30,000 at $37.09 on 2026-08-10, then exercised a further 82,500 on 08-11/12 without selling.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the Form 4s are public and the stock has already fallen 19% from the CEO's sale price. These are option exercises with sales, which is routine. The CEO's unsold exercises partly offset the signal, so the size is small.
findings.independence: The Form 4 excerpts (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000076267/000143774926028036/rdgdoc.xml) are the same documents.

outside_window.finding: Tulsa plant ($65m, production FY2029) and the ArianeGroup US C2B plant term sheet, with 100% of output allocated to Park. These are long-dated capacity items funded by the roughly $50m ATM, and none of the economics lands in the window.

searched_and_found_nothing: Company press releases since 2026-07-20 (zonebourse list): only dividend, VP appointment, CFO election and date notice. No pre-announcement and no guidance change.
EDGAR since 2026-07-01: the 8-K of 2026-09-28 is only a COO salary raise ($270k to $400k). No item 2.02, 1.01 or 4.02.
September/October FINRA short-interest settlements: none found published.
Cause of the roughly 19% drift from the August high: no company-specific cause found (filed as 0 per lessons).
GE Aerospace / Lockheed Q3 2026 prints: both report after the exit window.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Equity ATM of roughly $50m completed before the Q1 report (financing of Tulsa and the C2B capacity).
rejected_candidates.detail: Already complete and disclosed. The capex it funds is the outside_window Tulsa/Ariane item, and filing it separately would count the same capacity story twice.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with (null, OI 102). A mild positive lean sits against a stock 21% off its high with insider selling, and I cannot say the market is wrong about that drift, so p_up stays at 54.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 and the core table (lands inside what the company already guided): the GE H2 step-up rests on the company's own FY GE figure already stated on the call. Cut from +1.0 to +0.6.

Rule 5 (narrow proxy below the broad series): the Airbus August slowdown is sized below Hexcel's broader materials series, and the freight caveat lies inside the guided range. The merged negative was cut from -0.5 to -0.3, and Hexcel was cut from +0.5 to +0.4 as a proxy.
Rules 1/3 (public, mostly priced facts): the Lockheed multiyear was cut from +0.5 to +0.3, finance turnover from -0.3 to -0.2 and insider sales from -0.3 to -0.2.
Rule 8 (thin coverage) and the core 3b (a new Q3 guide is coming): abs_move raised from 8.0 to 8.5. p_up was left at 54.
